query: list of the best suv cars for teens
sources:
[1] New SUVs that are safe for your family and teen driver include the midsize 2015 Toyota Highlander, as well as the compact 2015 Mazda CX-5, Mitsubishi Outlander (AWD only) and Subaru Forester. These SUVs are both IIHS Top Safety Pick+ recipients and have NHTSA's highest five-star overall rating.

[2] Safest Cars for Teens: SUVs. If a large, dull sedan isn't your teen's ideal first car, McCartt suggests shopping for an SUV. With ESC dramatically reducing rollover risk, the inherent advantages offered by SUVs' greater size, weight and height emerge more clearly, the IIHS says in its January 2015 status report.

[3] As icing on the proverbial cake, each of the models on the best cars for teen drivers list carries reasonably low car-insurance rates – or at least as far as teen drivers are concerned.

[4] We selected the 15 cars on this list the pillars of safety, reliability, and affordability. And despite what you might expect, not all the cars are compact and midsize sedans. A number of models, including large SUVs and a few sports cars, are suitable choices for first-time drivers.

[5] Toyota Celica. For many teens, owning a sports car is nothing more than a distant dream. But parents and teens can find the ultimate compromise in the Toyota Celica. Once they get over the shock of seeing a cassette player for the first time, teens will enjoy this car just as much as their parents did.

[6] Lifestyle 7/18/2014 @ 8:32PM 85,728 views. The Safest Used Cars For Teen Drivers. Teenagers are more likely than other drivers to have the least safe types of cars, often ending up behind the wheel of vehicles that are old, small and without good crash protection. Those are the findings of new research conducted by the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety, a nonprofit financed by the insurance industry.

[7] [Slideshow: Safest Cars for Teens] Teens that have their own vehicle drive their vehicle more and are more likely to be in a crash, just because of that, says Anne McCartt, senior vice president of research at the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety.

[8] To that end, the experts at CarInsurance.com recently compiled a list of 14 used cars that should be ideal for teen drivers; we’re featuring them in the accompanying slideshow with our own commentary. Each is from the 2009 model year and is valued at $15,000 or less according to Edmunds.com.

[9] Earlier this week the group released a list of recommended used vehicles to help parents buy safe cars within their budgets, ranging from less than $5,000 to nearly $20,000. “A teenager’s first car is more than just a financial decision,” Adrian Lund, the institute’s president, said in a statement.

[10] Note that pickups and sport-utility vehicles were deliberately left off the list of best cars for teen drivers for apparent safety concerns. “While some pickups and SUVs score well, they’re really not great choices for novice drivers,” says CarInsurance.com consumer analyst Penny Gusner.

[2] Milk, yogurt, and cheese are rich natural sources of calcium and are the major food contributors of this nutrient to people in the United States [ 1 ]. Nondairy sources include vegetables, such as Chinese cabbage, kale, and broccoli. Spinach provides calcium, but its bioavailability is poor.

[3] Here are 5 of the best natural sources of calcium for healthy bones. Collard Greens. Leafy green vegetables are one of the most healthful sources of calcium and magnesium. One cup of boiled collards contains a whopping 358 milligrams.

[4] Here are 5 of the best natural sources of calcium for healthy bones. Collard Greens. Leafy green vegetables are one of the most healthful sources of calcium and magnesium. One cup of boiled collards contains a whopping 358 milligrams. Kale, broccoli, Swiss chard, bok choy and turnip greens are full of calcium, too.

[5] Food. Milk, yogurt, and cheese are rich natural sources of calcium and are the major food contributors of this nutrient to people in the United States [ 1 ]. Nondairy sources include vegetables, such as Chinese cabbage, kale, and broccoli.

[6] Milk and dairy products are some of the best food sources of calcium. These include milk, yogurt, and cheese. Broccoli helps to increase the intake of calcium, and is thus a very good source of calcium. Certain foods such as fruit juices and drinks, cereals, and tofu, are fortified with calcium.

[7] However, other excellent sources of calcium exist. Sources of well-absorbed calcium for vegans include calcium-fortified soy milk and juice, calcium-set tofu, soybeans and soynuts, bok choy, broccoli, collards, Chinese cabbage, kale, mustard greens, and okra.

[8] Sources of Calcium. Food. Milk, yogurt, and cheese are rich natural sources of calcium and are the major food contributors of this nutrient to people in the United States [ 1 ]. Nondairy sources include vegetables, such as Chinese cabbage, kale, and broccoli.

[9] Calcium supplements offer a good source of calcium and help protect bones and teeth. Most commonly, calcium is present in supplements mainly in the form of carbonates and citrates. It is also present in supplements or certain fortified foods in the form of phosphates, gluconates, and lactates, to some extent.

[10] Here are 5 of the best natural sources of calcium for healthy bones. Collard Greens. Leafy green vegetables are one of the most healthful sources of calcium and magnesium.

query: list of the best suv cars for teens
sources:
[1] New SUVs that are safe for your family and teen driver include the midsize 2015 Toyota Highlander, as well as the compact 2015 Mazda CX-5, Mitsubishi Outlander (AWD only) and Subaru Forester. These SUVs are both IIHS Top Safety Pick+ recipients and have NHTSA's highest five-star overall rating.

[2] Safest Cars for Teens: SUVs. If a large, dull sedan isn't your teen's ideal first car, McCartt suggests shopping for an SUV. With ESC dramatically reducing rollover risk, the inherent advantages offered by SUVs' greater size, weight and height emerge more clearly, the IIHS says in its January 2015 status report.

[3] As icing on the proverbial cake, each of the models on the best cars for teen drivers list carries reasonably low car-insurance rates – or at least as far as teen drivers are concerned.

[4] We selected the 15 cars on this list the pillars of safety, reliability, and affordability. And despite what you might expect, not all the cars are compact and midsize sedans. A number of models, including large SUVs and a few sports cars, are suitable choices for first-time drivers.

[5] Toyota Celica. For many teens, owning a sports car is nothing more than a distant dream. But parents and teens can find the ultimate compromise in the Toyota Celica. Once they get over the shock of seeing a cassette player for the first time, teens will enjoy this car just as much as their parents did.

[6] Lifestyle 7/18/2014 @ 8:32PM 85,728 views. The Safest Used Cars For Teen Drivers. Teenagers are more likely than other drivers to have the least safe types of cars, often ending up behind the wheel of vehicles that are old, small and without good crash protection. Those are the findings of new research conducted by the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety, a nonprofit financed by the insurance industry.

[7] [Slideshow: Safest Cars for Teens] Teens that have their own vehicle drive their vehicle more and are more likely to be in a crash, just because of that, says Anne McCartt, senior vice president of research at the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety.

[8] To that end, the experts at CarInsurance.com recently compiled a list of 14 used cars that should be ideal for teen drivers; we’re featuring them in the accompanying slideshow with our own commentary. Each is from the 2009 model year and is valued at $15,000 or less according to Edmunds.com.

[9] Earlier this week the group released a list of recommended used vehicles to help parents buy safe cars within their budgets, ranging from less than $5,000 to nearly $20,000. “A teenager’s first car is more than just a financial decision,” Adrian Lund, the institute’s president, said in a statement.

[10] Note that pickups and sport-utility vehicles were deliberately left off the list of best cars for teen drivers for apparent safety concerns. “While some pickups and SUVs score well, they’re really not great choices for novice drivers,” says CarInsurance.com consumer analyst Penny Gusner.

[1] Collard Greens. Leafy green vegetables are one of the most healthful sources of calcium and magnesium. One cup of boiled collards contains a whopping 358 milligrams. Kale, broccoli, Swiss chard, bok choy and turnip greens are full of calcium, too.

[2] Milk, yogurt, and cheese are rich natural sources of calcium and are the major food contributors of this nutrient to people in the United States [ 1 ]. Nondairy sources include vegetables, such as Chinese cabbage, kale, and broccoli. Spinach provides calcium, but its bioavailability is poor.

[7] However, other excellent sources of calcium exist. Sources of well-absorbed calcium for vegans include calcium-fortified soy milk and juice, calcium-set tofu, soybeans and soynuts, bok choy, broccoli, collards, Chinese cabbage, kale, mustard greens, and okra.

query: best natural sources of calcium
sources:
[1] Collard Greens. Leafy green vegetables are one of the most healthful sources of calcium and magnesium. One cup of boiled collards contains a whopping 358 milligrams. Kale, broccoli, Swiss chard, bok choy and turnip greens are full of calcium, too.

[2] Milk, yogurt, and cheese are rich natural sources of calcium and are the major food contributors of this nutrient to people in the United States [ 1 ]. Nondairy sources include vegetables, such as Chinese cabbage, kale, and broccoli. Spinach provides calcium, but its bioavailability is poor.

[3] Here are 5 of the best natural sources of calcium for healthy bones. Collard Greens. Leafy green vegetables are one of the most healthful sources of calcium and magnesium. One cup of boiled collards contains a whopping 358 milligrams.

[4] Here are 5 of the best natural sources of calcium for healthy bones. Collard Greens. Leafy green vegetables are one of the most healthful sources of calcium and magnesium. One cup of boiled collards contains a whopping 358 milligrams. Kale, broccoli, Swiss chard, bok choy and turnip greens are full of calcium, too.

[5] Food. Milk, yogurt, and cheese are rich natural sources of calcium and are the major food contributors of this nutrient to people in the United States [ 1 ]. Nondairy sources include vegetables, such as Chinese cabbage, kale, and broccoli.

[6] Milk and dairy products are some of the best food sources of calcium. These include milk, yogurt, and cheese. Broccoli helps to increase the intake of calcium, and is thus a very good source of calcium. Certain foods such as fruit juices and drinks, cereals, and tofu, are fortified with calcium.

[7] However, other excellent sources of calcium exist. Sources of well-absorbed calcium for vegans include calcium-fortified soy milk and juice, calcium-set tofu, soybeans and soynuts, bok choy, broccoli, collards, Chinese cabbage, kale, mustard greens, and okra.

[8] Sources of Calcium. Food. Milk, yogurt, and cheese are rich natural sources of calcium and are the major food contributors of this nutrient to people in the United States [ 1 ]. Nondairy sources include vegetables, such as Chinese cabbage, kale, and broccoli.

[9] Calcium supplements offer a good source of calcium and help protect bones and teeth. Most commonly, calcium is present in supplements mainly in the form of carbonates and citrates. It is also present in supplements or certain fortified foods in the form of phosphates, gluconates, and lactates, to some extent.

[10] Here are 5 of the best natural sources of calcium for healthy bones. Collard Greens. Leafy green vegetables are one of the most healthful sources of calcium and magnesium.

query: list of the best suv cars for teens
sources:
[1] New SUVs that are safe for your family and teen driver include the midsize 2015 Toyota Highlander, as well as the compact 2015 Mazda CX-5, Mitsubishi Outlander (AWD only) and Subaru Forester. These SUVs are both IIHS Top Safety Pick+ recipients and have NHTSA's highest five-star overall rating.

[2] Safest Cars for Teens: SUVs. If a large, dull sedan isn't your teen's ideal first car, McCartt suggests shopping for an SUV. With ESC dramatically reducing rollover risk, the inherent advantages offered by SUVs' greater size, weight and height emerge more clearly, the IIHS says in its January 2015 status report.

[3] As icing on the proverbial cake, each of the models on the best cars for teen drivers list carries reasonably low car-insurance rates – or at least as far as teen drivers are concerned.

[4] We selected the 15 cars on this list the pillars of safety, reliability, and affordability. And despite what you might expect, not all the cars are compact and midsize sedans. A number of models, including large SUVs and a few sports cars, are suitable choices for first-time drivers.

[5] Toyota Celica. For many teens, owning a sports car is nothing more than a distant dream. But parents and teens can find the ultimate compromise in the Toyota Celica. Once they get over the shock of seeing a cassette player for the first time, teens will enjoy this car just as much as their parents did.

[6] Lifestyle 7/18/2014 @ 8:32PM 85,728 views. The Safest Used Cars For Teen Drivers. Teenagers are more likely than other drivers to have the least safe types of cars, often ending up behind the wheel of vehicles that are old, small and without good crash protection. Those are the findings of new research conducted by the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety, a nonprofit financed by the insurance industry.

[7] [Slideshow: Safest Cars for Teens] Teens that have their own vehicle drive their vehicle more and are more likely to be in a crash, just because of that, says Anne McCartt, senior vice president of research at the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety.

[8] To that end, the experts at CarInsurance.com recently compiled a list of 14 used cars that should be ideal for teen drivers; we’re featuring them in the accompanying slideshow with our own commentary. Each is from the 2009 model year and is valued at $15,000 or less according to Edmunds.com.

[9] Earlier this week the group released a list of recommended used vehicles to help parents buy safe cars within their budgets, ranging from less than $5,000 to nearly $20,000. “A teenager’s first car is more than just a financial decision,” Adrian Lund, the institute’s president, said in a statement.

[10] Note that pickups and sport-utility vehicles were deliberately left off the list of best cars for teen drivers for apparent safety concerns. “While some pickups and SUVs score well, they’re really not great choices for novice drivers,” says CarInsurance.com consumer analyst Penny Gusner.

query: best natural sources of calcium
sources:
[1] Collard Greens. Leafy green vegetables are one of the most healthful sources of calcium and magnesium. One cup of boiled collards contains a whopping 358 milligrams. Kale, broccoli, Swiss chard, bok choy and turnip greens are full of calcium, too.

[2] Milk, yogurt, and cheese are rich natural sources of calcium and are the major food contributors of this nutrient to people in the United States [ 1 ]. Nondairy sources include vegetables, such as Chinese cabbage, kale, and broccoli. Spinach provides calcium, but its bioavailability is poor.

[3] Here are 5 of the best natural sources of calcium for healthy bones. Collard Greens. Leafy green vegetables are one of the most healthful sources of calcium and magnesium. One cup of boiled collards contains a whopping 358 milligrams.

[4] Here are 5 of the best natural sources of calcium for healthy bones. Collard Greens. Leafy green vegetables are one of the most healthful sources of calcium and magnesium. Broccoli helps to increase the intake of calcium, and is thus a very good source of calcium. Certain foods such as fruit juices and drinks, cereals, and tofu, are fortified with calcium.

[7] However, other excellent sources of calcium exist. Sources of well-absorbed calcium for vegans include calcium-fortified soy milk and juice, calcium-set tofu, soybeans and soynuts, bok choy, broccoli, collards, Chinese cabbage, kale, mustard greens, and okra.

[8] Sources of Calcium. Food. Milk, yogurt, and cheese are rich natural sources of calcium and are the major food contributors of this nutrient to people in the United States [ 1 ]. Nondairy sources include vegetables, such as Chinese cabbage, kale, and broccoli.

[9] Calcium supplements offer a good source of calcium and help protect bones and teeth. Most commonly, calcium is present in supplements mainly in the form of carbonates and citrates. query: list of the best suv cars for teens
sources:
[1] New SUVs that are safe for your family and teen driver include the midsize 2015 Toyota Highlander, as well as the compact 2015 Mazda CX-5, Mitsubishi Outlander (AWD only) and Subaru Forester. These SUVs are both IIHS Top Safety Pick+ recipients and have NHTSA's highest five-star overall rating.

[2] Safest Cars for Teens: SUVs. If a large, dull sedan isn't your teen's ideal first car, McCartt suggests shopping for an SUV. With ESC dramatically reducing rollover risk, the inherent advantages offered by SUVs' greater size, weight and height emerge more clearly, the IIHS says in its January 2015 status report.

[3] As icing on the proverbial cake, each of the models on the best cars for teen drivers list carries reasonably low car-insurance rates – or at least as far as teen drivers are concerned.

[4] We selected the 15 cars on this list the pillars of safety, reliability, and affordability. And despite what you might expect, not all the cars are compact and midsize sedans. A number of models, including large SUVs and a few sports cars, are suitable choices for first-time drivers.

[5] Toyota Celica. For many teens, owning a sports car is nothing more than a distant dream. But parents and teens can find the ultimate compromise in the Toyota Celica. Once they get over the shock of seeing a cassette player for the first time, teens will enjoy this car just as much as their parents did.

[6] Lifestyle 7/18/2014 @ 8:32PM 85,728 views. The Safest Used Cars For Teen Drivers. Teenagers are more likely than other drivers to have the least safe types of cars, often ending up behind the wheel of vehicles that are old, small and without good crash protection. Those are the findings of new research conducted by the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety, a nonprofit financed by the insurance industry.

[7] [Slideshow: Safest Cars for Teens] Teens that have their own vehicle drive their vehicle more and are more likely to be in a crash, just because of that, says Anne McCartt, senior vice president of research at the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety.

[8] To that end, the experts at CarInsurance.com recently compiled a list of 14 used cars that should be ideal for teen drivers; we’re featuring them in the accompanying slideshow with our own commentary. Each is from the 2009 model year and is valued at $15,000 or less according to Edmunds.com.

[9] Earlier this week the group released a list of recommended used vehicles to help parents buy safe cars within their budgets, ranging from less than $5,000 to nearly $20,000. “A teenager’s first car is more than just a financial decision,” Adrian Lund, the institute’s president, said in a statement.

[10] Note that pickups and sport-utility vehicles were deliberately left off the list of best cars for teen drivers for apparent safety concerns. “While some pickups and SUVs score well, they’re really not great choices for novice drivers,” says CarInsurance.com consumer analyst Penny Gusner.

[2] Milk, yogurt, and cheese are rich natural sources of calcium and are the major food contributors of this nutrient to people in the United States [ 1 ]. Nondairy sources include vegetables, such as Chinese cabbage, kale, and broccoli. Spinach provides calcium, but its bioavailability is poor.

[2] Milk, yogurt, and cheese are rich natural sources of calcium and are the major food contributors of this nutrient to people in the United States [ 1 ]. Nondairy sources include vegetables, such as Chinese cabbage, kale, and broccoli. Spinach provides calcium, but its bioavailability is poor.

query: list of the best suv cars for teens
sources:
[1] New SUVs that are safe for your family and teen driver include the midsize 2015 Toyota Highlander, as well as the compact 2015 Mazda CX-5, Mitsubishi Outlander (AWD only) and Subaru Forester. These SUVs are both IIHS Top Safety Pick+ recipients and have NHTSA's highest five-star overall rating.

[2] Safest Cars for Teens: SUVs. If a large, dull sedan isn't your teen's ideal first car, McCartt suggests shopping for an SUV. With ESC dramatically reducing rollover risk, the inherent advantages offered by SUVs' greater size, weight and height emerge more clearly, the IIHS says in its January 2015 status report.

[3] As icing on the proverbial cake, each of the models on the best cars for teen drivers list carries reasonably low car-insurance rates – or at least as far as teen drivers are concerned.

[4] We selected the 15 cars on this list the pillars of safety, reliability, and affordability. And despite what you might expect, not all the cars are compact and midsize sedans. A number of models, including large SUVs and a few sports cars, are suitable choices for first-time drivers.

[5] Toyota Celica. For many teens, owning a sports car is nothing more than a distant dream. But parents and teens can find the ultimate compromise in the Toyota Celica. Once they get over the shock of seeing a cassette player for the first time, teens will enjoy this car just as much as their parents did.

[6] Lifestyle 7/18/2014 @ 8:32PM 85,728 views. The Safest Used Cars For Teen Drivers. Teenagers are more likely than other drivers to have the least safe types of cars, often ending up behind the wheel of vehicles that are old, small and without good crash protection. Those are the findings of new research conducted by the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety, a nonprofit financed by the insurance industry.

[7] [Slideshow: Safest Cars for Teens] Teens that have their own vehicle drive their vehicle more and are more likely to be in a crash, just because of that, says Anne McCartt, senior vice president of research at the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety.

[8] To that end, the experts at CarInsurance.com recently compiled a list of 14 used cars that should be ideal for teen drivers; we’re featuring them in the accompanying slideshow with our own commentary. Each is from the 2009 model year and is valued at $15,000 or less according to Edmunds.com.

[9] Earlier this week the group released a list of recommended used vehicles to help parents buy safe cars within their budgets, ranging from less than $5,000 to nearly $20,000. “A teenager’s first car is more than just a financial decision,” Adrian Lund, the institute’s president, said in a statement.

[10] Note that pickups and sport-utility vehicles were deliberately left off the list of best cars for teen drivers for apparent safety concerns. “While some pickups and SUVs score well, they’re really not great choices for novice drivers,” says CarInsurance.com consumer analyst Penny Gusner.

query: list of the best suv cars for teens
sources:
[1] New SUVs that are safe for your family and teen driver include the midsize 2015 Toyota Highlander, as well as the compact 2015 Mazda CX-5, Mitsubishi Outlander (AWD only) and Subaru Forester. These SUVs are both IIHS Top Safety Pick+ recipients and have NHTSA's highest five-star overall rating.

[2] Safest Cars for Teens: SUVs. If a large, dull sedan isn't your teen's ideal first car, McCartt suggests shopping for an SUV. With ESC dramatically reducing rollover risk, the inherent advantages offered by SUVs' greater size, weight and height emerge more clearly, the IIHS says in its January 2015 status report.

[3] As icing on the proverbial cake, each of the models on the best cars for teen drivers list carries reasonably low car-insurance rates – or at least as far as teen drivers are concerned.

[4] We selected the 15 cars on this list the pillars of safety, reliability, and affordability. And despite what you might expect, not all the cars are compact and midsize sedans. A number of models, including large SUVs and a few sports cars, are suitable choices for first-time drivers.

[5] Toyota Celica. For many teens, owning a sports car is nothing more than a distant dream. But parents and teens can find the ultimate compromise in the Toyota Celica. Once they get over the shock of seeing a cassette player for the first time, teens will enjoy this car just as much as their parents did.

[6] Lifestyle 7/18/2014 @ 8:32PM 85,728 views. The Safest Used Cars For Teen Drivers. Teenagers are more likely than other drivers to have the least safe types of cars, often ending up behind the wheel of vehicles that are old, small and without good crash protection. Those are the findings of new research conducted by the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety, a nonprofit financed by the insurance industry.

[7] [Slideshow: Safest Cars for Teens] Teens that have their own vehicle drive their vehicle more and are more likely to be in a crash, just because of that, says Anne McCartt, senior vice president of research at the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety.

[8] To that end, the experts at CarInsurance.com recently compiled a list of 14 used cars that should be ideal for teen drivers; we’re featuring them in the accompanying slideshow with our own commentary. Each is from the 2009 model year and is valued at $15,000 or less according to Edmunds.com.

[9] Earlier this week the group released a list of recommended used vehicles to help parents buy safe cars within their budgets, ranging from less than $5,000 to nearly $20,000. “A teenager’s first car is more than just a financial decision,” Adrian Lund, the institute’s president, said in a statement.

[10] Note that pickups and sport-utility vehicles were deliberately left off the list of best cars for teen drivers for apparent safety concerns. “While some pickups and SUVs score well, they’re really not great choices for novice drivers,” says CarInsurance.com consumer analyst Penny Gusner.

[7] [Slideshow: Safest Cars for Teens] Teens that have their own vehicle drive their vehicle more and are more likely to be in a crash, just because of that, says Anne McCartt, senior vice president of research at the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety.

[8] To that end, the experts at CarInsurance.com recently compiled a list of 14 used cars that should be ideal for teen drivers; we’re featuring them in the accompanying slideshow with our own commentary. Each is from the 2009 model year and is valued at $15,000 or less according to Edmunds.com.

[9] Earlier this week the group released a list of recommended used vehicles to help parents buy safe cars within their budgets, ranging from less than $5,000 to nearly $20,000. “A teenager’s first car is more than just a financial decision,” Adrian Lund, the institute’s president, said in a statement.

[10] Note that pickups and sport-utility vehicles were deliberately left off the list of best cars for teen drivers for apparent safety concerns. “While some pickups and SUVs score well, they’re really not great choices for novice drivers,” says CarInsurance.com consumer analyst Penny Gusner.

query: list of the best suv cars for teens
sources:
[1] New SUVs that are safe for your family and teen driver include the midsize 2015 Toyota Highlander, as well as the compact 2015 Mazda CX-5, Mitsubishi Outlander (AWD only) and Subaru Forester. These SUVs are both IIHS Top Safety Pick+ recipients and have NHTSA's highest five-star overall rating.

[2] Safest Cars for Teens: SUVs. If a large, dull sedan isn't your teen's ideal first car, McCartt suggests shopping for an SUV. With ESC dramatically reducing rollover risk, the inherent advantages offered by SUVs' greater size, weight and height emerge more clearly, the IIHS says in its January 2015 status report.

[3] As icing on the proverbial cake, each of the models on the best cars for teen drivers list carries reasonably low car-insurance rates – or at least as far as teen drivers are concerned.

[4] We selected the 15 cars on this list the pillars of safety, reliability, and affordability. And despite what you might expect, not all the cars are compact and midsize sedans. A number of models, including large SUVs and a few sports cars, are suitable choices for first-time drivers.

[5] Toyota Celica. For many teens, owning a sports car is nothing more than a distant dream. But parents and teens can find the ultimate compromise in the Toyota Celica. Once they get over the shock of seeing a cassette player for the first time, teens will enjoy this car just as much as their parents did.

[6] Lifestyle 7/18/2014 @ 8:32PM 85,728 views. The Safest Used Cars For Teen Drivers. Teenagers are more likely than other drivers to have the least safe types of cars, often ending up behind the wheel of vehicles that are old, small and without good crash protection. Those are the findings of new research conducted by the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety, a nonprofit financed by the insurance industry.

[7] [Slideshow: Safest Cars for Teens] Teens that have their own vehicle drive their vehicle more and are more likely to be in a crash, just because of that, says Anne McCartt, senior vice president of research at the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety.

[8] To that end, the experts at CarInsurance.com recently compiled a list of 14 used cars that should be ideal for teen drivers; we’re featuring them in the accompanying slideshow with our own commentary. Each is from the 2009 model year and is valued at $15,000 or less according to Edmunds.com.

[9] Earlier this week the group released a list of recommended used vehicles to help parents buy safe cars within their budgets, ranging from less than $5,000 to nearly $20,000. “A teenager’s first car is more than just a financial decision,” Adrian Lund, the institute’s president, said in a statement.

[10] Note that pickups and sport-utility vehicles were deliberately left off the list of best cars for teen drivers for apparent safety concerns. “While some pickups and SUVs score well, they’re really not great choices for novice drivers,” says CarInsurance.com consumer analyst Penny Gusner.

query: list of the best suv cars for teens
sources:
[1] New SUVs that are safe for your family and teen driver include the midsize 2015 Toyota Highlander, as well as the compact 2015 Mazda CX-5, Mitsubishi Outlander (AWD only) and Subaru Forester. These SUVs are both IIHS Top Safety Pick+ recipients and have NHTSA's highest five-star overall rating.

[2] Safest Cars for Teens: SUVs. If a large, dull sedan isn't your teen's ideal first car, McCartt suggests shopping for an SUV. With ESC dramatically reducing rollover risk, the inherent advantages offered by SUVs' greater size, weight and height emerge more clearly, the IIHS says in its January 2015 status report.

[3] As icing on the proverbial cake, each of the models on the best cars for teen drivers list carries reasonably low car-insurance rates – or at least as far as teen drivers are concerned.

[4] We selected the 15 cars on this list the pillars of safety, reliability, and affordability. And despite what you might expect, not all the cars are compact and midsize sedans. A number of models, including large SUVs and a few sports cars, are suitable choices for first-time drivers.

[5] Toyota Celica. For many teens, owning a sports car is nothing more than a distant dream. But parents and teens can find the ultimate compromise in the Toyota Celica. Once they get over the shock of seeing a cassette player for the first time, teens will enjoy this car just as much as their parents did.

[6] Lifestyle 7/18/2014 @ 8:32PM 85,728 views. The Safest Used Cars For Teen Drivers. Teenagers are more likely than other drivers to have the least safe types of cars, often ending up behind the wheel of vehicles that are old, small and without good crash protection. Those are the findings of new research conducted by the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety, a nonprofit financed by the insurance industry.

[7] [Slideshow: Safest Cars for Teens] Teens that have their own vehicle drive their vehicle more and are more likely to be in a crash, just because of that, says Anne McCartt, senior vice president of research at the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety.

[8] To that end, the experts at CarInsurance.com recently compiled a list of 14 used cars that should be ideal for teen drivers; we’re featuring them in the accompanying slideshow with our own commentary. Each is from the 2009 model year and is valued at $15,000 or less according to Edmunds.com.

[9] Earlier this week the group released a list of recommended used vehicles to help parents buy safe cars within their budgets, ranging from less than $5,000 to nearly $20,000. “A teenager’s first car is more than just a financial decision,” Adrian Lund, the institute’s president, said in a statement.

[10] Note that pickups and sport-utility vehicles were deliberately left off the list of best cars for teen drivers for apparent safety concerns. “While some pickups and SUVs score well, they’re really not great choices for novice drivers,” says CarInsurance.com consumer analyst Penny Gusner.

sources:
[1] Collard Greens. Leafy green vegetables are one of the most healthful sources of calcium and magnesium. One cup of boiled collards contains a whopping 358 milligrams. Kale, broccoli, Swiss chard, bok choy and turnip greens are full of calcium, too.

[2] Milk, yogurt, and cheese are rich natural sources of calcium and are the major food contributors of this nutrient to people in the United States [ 1 ]. Nondairy sources include vegetables, such as Chinese cabbage, kale, and broccoli. Spinach provides calcium, but its bioavailability is poor.

Broccoli helps to increase the intake of calcium, and is thus a very good source of calcium. Certain foods such as fruit juices and drinks, cereals, and tofu, are fortified with calcium.

[7] However, other excellent sources of calcium exist. Sources of well-absorbed calcium for vegans include calcium-fortified soy milk and juice, calcium-set tofu, soybeans and soynuts, bok choy, broccoli, collards, Chinese cabbage, kale, mustard greens, and okra.

[2] Milk, yogurt, and cheese are rich natural sources of calcium and are the major food contributors of this nutrient to people in the United States [ 1 ]. Nondairy sources include vegetables, such as Chinese cabbage, kale, and broccoli. Spinach provides calcium, but its bioavailability is poor.

[7] However, other excellent sources of calcium exist. Sources of well-absorbed calcium for vegans include calcium-fortified soy milk and juice, calcium-set tofu, soybeans and soynuts, bok choy, broccoli, collards, Chinese cabbage, kale, mustard greens, and okra.

query: list of the best suv cars for teens
sources:
[1] New SUVs that are safe for your family and teen driver include the midsize 2015 Toyota Highlander, as well as the compact 2015 Mazda CX-5, Mitsubishi Outlander (AWD only) and Subaru Forester. These SUVs are both IIHS Top Safety Pick+ recipients and have NHTSA's highest five-star overall rating.

[2] Safest Cars for Teens: SUVs. If a large, dull sedan isn't your teen's ideal first car, McCartt suggests shopping for an SUV. With ESC dramatically reducing rollover risk, the inherent advantages offered by SUVs' greater size, weight and height emerge more clearly, the IIHS says in its January 2015 status report.

[3] As icing on the proverbial cake, each of the models on the best cars for teen drivers list carries reasonably low car-insurance rates – or at least as far as teen drivers are concerned.

[4] We selected the 15 cars on this list the pillars of safety, reliability, and affordability. And despite what you might expect, not all the cars are compact and midsize sedans. A number of models, including large SUVs and a few sports cars, are suitable choices for first-time drivers.

[5] Toyota Celica. For many teens, owning a sports car is nothing more than a distant dream. But parents and teens can find the ultimate compromise in the Toyota Celica. Once they get over the shock of seeing a cassette player for the first time, teens will enjoy this car just as much as their parents did.

[6] Lifestyle 7/18/2014 @ 8:32PM 85,728 views. The Safest Used Cars For Teen Drivers. Teenagers are more likely than other drivers to have the least safe types of cars, often ending up behind the wheel of vehicles that are old, small and without good crash protection. Those are the findings of new research conducted by the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety, a nonprofit financed by the insurance industry.

[7] [Slideshow: Safest Cars for Teens] Teens that have their own vehicle drive their vehicle more and are more likely to be in a crash, just because of that, says Anne McCartt, senior vice president of research at the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety.

[8] To that end, the experts at CarInsurance.com recently compiled a list of 14 used cars that should be ideal for teen drivers; we’re featuring them in the accompanying slideshow with our own commentary. Each is from the 2009 model year and is valued at $15,000 or less according to Edmunds.com.

[9] Earlier this week the group released a list of recommended used vehicles to help parents buy safe cars within their budgets, ranging from less than $5,000 to nearly $20,000. “A teenager’s first car is more than just a financial decision,” Adrian Lund, the institute’s president, said in a statement.

[10] Note that pickups and sport-utility vehicles were deliberately left off the list of best cars for teen drivers for apparent safety concerns. “While some pickups and SUVs score well, they’re really not great choices for novice drivers,” says CarInsurance.com consumer analyst Penny Gusner.

[1] Collard Greens. Leafy green vegetables are one of the most healthful sources of calcium and magnesium. One cup of boiled collards contains a whopping 358 milligrams. Kale, broccoli, Swiss chard, bok choy and turnip greens are full of calcium, too.

[2] Milk, yogurt, and cheese are rich natural sources of calcium and are the major food contributors of this nutrient to people in the United States [ 1 ]. Nondairy sources include vegetables, such as Chinese cabbage, kale, and broccoli. Spinach provides calcium, but its bioavailability is poor.

query: list of the best suv cars for teens
sources:
[1] New SUVs that are safe for your family and teen driver include the midsize 2015 Toyota Highlander, as well as the compact 2015 Mazda CX-5, Mitsubishi Outlander (AWD only) and Subaru Forester. These SUVs are both IIHS Top Safety Pick+ recipients and have NHTSA's highest five-star overall rating.

[2] Safest Cars for Teens: SUVs. If a large, dull sedan isn't your teen's ideal first car, McCartt suggests shopping for an SUV. With ESC dramatically reducing rollover risk, the inherent advantages offered by SUVs' greater size, weight and height emerge more clearly, the IIHS says in its January 2015 status report.

[3] As icing on the proverbial cake, each of the models on the best cars for teen drivers list carries reasonably low car-insurance rates – or at least as far as teen drivers are concerned.

[4] We selected the 15 cars on this list the pillars of safety, reliability, and affordability. And despite what you might expect, not all the cars are compact and midsize sedans. A number of models, including large SUVs and a few sports cars, are suitable choices for first-time drivers.

[5] Toyota Celica. For many teens, owning a sports car is nothing more than a distant dream. But parents and teens can find the ultimate compromise in the Toyota Celica. Once they get over the shock of seeing a cassette player for the first time, teens will enjoy this car just as much as their parents did.

[6] Lifestyle 7/18/2014 @ 8:32PM 85,728 views. The Safest Used Cars For Teen Drivers. Teenagers are more likely than other drivers to have the least safe types of cars, often ending up behind the wheel of vehicles that are old, small and without good crash protection. Those are the findings of new research conducted by the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety, a nonprofit financed by the insurance industry.

[7] [Slideshow: Safest Cars for Teens] Teens that have their own vehicle drive their vehicle more and are more likely to be in a crash, just because of that, says Anne McCartt, senior vice president of research at the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety.

[8] To that end, the experts at CarInsurance.com recently compiled a list of 14 used cars that should be ideal for teen drivers; we’re featuring them in the accompanying slideshow with our own commentary. Each is from the 2009 model year and is valued at $15,000 or less according to Edmunds.com.

[9] Earlier this week the group released a list of recommended used vehicles to help parents buy safe cars within their budgets, ranging from less than $5,000 to nearly $20,000. “A teenager’s first car is more than just a financial decision,” Adrian Lund, the institute’s president, said in a statement.

[10] Note that pickups and sport-utility vehicles were deliberately left off the list of best cars for teen drivers for apparent safety concerns. “While some pickups and SUVs score well, they’re really not great choices for novice drivers,” says CarInsurance.com consumer analyst Penny Gusner.

query: list of the best suv cars for teens
sources:
[1] New SUVs that are safe for your family and teen driver include the midsize 2015 Toyota Highlander, as well as the compact 2015 Mazda CX-5, Mitsubishi Outlander (AWD only) and Subaru Forester. These SUVs are both IIHS Top Safety Pick+ recipients and have NHTSA's highest five-star overall rating.

[2] Safest Cars for Teens: SUVs. If a large, dull sedan isn't your teen's ideal first car, McCartt suggests shopping for an SUV. With ESC dramatically reducing rollover risk, the inherent advantages offered by SUVs' greater size, weight and height emerge more clearly, the IIHS says in its January 2015 status report.

[3] As icing on the proverbial cake, each of the models on the best cars for teen drivers list carries reasonably low car-insurance rates – or at least as far as teen drivers are concerned.

[4] We selected the 15 cars on this list the pillars of safety, reliability, and affordability. And despite what you might expect, not all the cars are compact and midsize sedans. A number of models, including large SUVs and a few sports cars, are suitable choices for first-time drivers.

[5] Toyota Celica. For many teens, owning a sports car is nothing more than a distant dream. But parents and teens can find the ultimate compromise in the Toyota Celica. Once they get over the shock of seeing a cassette player for the first time, teens will enjoy this car just as much as their parents did.

[6] Lifestyle 7/18/2014 @ 8:32PM 85,728 views. The Safest Used Cars For Teen Drivers. Teenagers are more likely than other drivers to have the least safe types of cars, often ending up behind the wheel of vehicles that are old, small and without good crash protection. Those are the findings of new research conducted by the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety, a nonprofit financed by the insurance industry.

[7] [Slideshow: Safest Cars for Teens] Teens that have their own vehicle drive their vehicle more and are more likely to be in a crash, just because of that, says Anne McCartt, senior vice president of research at the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety.

[8] To that end, the experts at CarInsurance.com recently compiled a list of 14 used cars that should be ideal for teen drivers; we’re featuring them in the accompanying slideshow with our own commentary. Each is from the 2009 model year and is valued at $15,000 or less according to Edmunds.com.

[9] Earlier this week the group released a list of recommended used vehicles to help parents buy safe cars within their budgets, ranging from less than $5,000 to nearly $20,000. “A teenager’s first car is more than just a financial decision,” Adrian Lund, the institute’s president, said in a statement.

[10] Note that pickups and sport-utility vehicles were deliberately left off the list of best cars for teen drivers for apparent safety concerns. “While some pickups and SUVs score well, they’re really not great choices for novice drivers,” says CarInsurance.com consumer analyst Penny Gusner.

query: list of the best suv cars for teens
sources:
[1] New SUVs that are safe for your family and teen driver include the midsize 2015 Toyota Highlander, as well as the compact 2015 Mazda CX-5, Mitsubishi Outlander (AWD only) and Subaru Forester. These SUVs are both IIHS Top Safety Pick+ recipients and have NHTSA's highest five-star overall rating.

[2] Safest Cars for Teens: SUVs. If a large, dull sedan isn't your teen's ideal first car, McCartt suggests shopping for an SUV. With ESC dramatically reducing rollover risk, the inherent advantages offered by SUVs' greater size, weight and height emerge more clearly, the IIHS says in its January 2015 status report.

[3] As icing on the proverbial cake, each of the models on the best cars for teen drivers list carries reasonably low car-insurance rates – or at least as far as teen drivers are concerned.

[4] We selected the 15 cars on this list the pillars of safety, reliability, and affordability. And despite what you might expect, not all the cars are compact and midsize sedans. A number of models, including large SUVs and a few sports cars, are suitable choices for first-time drivers.

[5] Toyota Celica. For many teens, owning a sports car is nothing more than a distant dream. But parents and teens can find the ultimate compromise in the Toyota Celica. Once they get over the shock of seeing a cassette player for the first time, teens will enjoy this car just as much as their parents did.

[6] Lifestyle 7/18/2014 @ 8:32PM 85,728 views. The Safest Used Cars For Teen Drivers. Teenagers are more likely than other drivers to have the least safe types of cars, often ending up behind the wheel of vehicles that are old, small and without good crash protection. Those are the findings of new research conducted by the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety, a nonprofit financed by the insurance industry.

[7] [Slideshow: Safest Cars for Teens] Teens that have their own vehicle drive their vehicle more and are more likely to be in a crash, just because of that, says Anne McCartt, senior vice president of research at the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety.

[8] To that end, the experts at CarInsurance.com recently compiled a list of 14 used cars that should be ideal for teen drivers; we’re featuring them in the accompanying slideshow with our own commentary. Each is from the 2009 model year and is valued at $15,000 or less according to Edmunds.com.

[9] Earlier this week the group released a list of recommended used vehicles to help parents buy safe cars within their budgets, ranging from less than $5,000 to nearly $20,000. “A teenager’s first car is more than just a financial decision,” Adrian Lund, the institute’s president, said in a statement.

[10] Note that pickups and sport-utility vehicles were deliberately left off the list of best cars for teen drivers for apparent safety concerns. “While some pickups and SUVs score well, they’re really not great choices for novice drivers,” says CarInsurance.com consumer analyst Penny Gusner.

[9] Calcium supplements offer a good source of calcium and help protect bones and teeth. Most commonly, calcium is present in supplements mainly in the form of carbonates and citrates. It is also present in supplements or certain fortified foods in the form of phosphates, gluconates, and lactates, to some extent.

[10] Here are 5 of the best natural sources of calcium for healthy bones. Collard Greens. Leafy green vegetables are one of the most healthful sources of calcium and magnesium.

[7] [Slideshow: Safest Cars for Teens] Teens that have their own vehicle drive their vehicle more and are more likely to be in a crash, just because of that, says Anne McCartt, senior vice president of research at the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety.

[8] To that end, the experts at CarInsurance.com recently compiled a list of 14 used cars that should be ideal for teen drivers; we’re featuring them in the accompanying slideshow with our own commentary. Each is from the 2009 model year and is valued at $15,000 or less according to Edmunds.com.

[9] Earlier this week the group released a list of recommended used vehicles to help parents buy safe cars within their budgets, ranging from less than $5,000 to nearly $20,000. “A teenager’s first car is more than just a financial decision,” Adrian Lund, the institute’s president, said in a statement.

[10] Note that pickups and sport-utility vehicles were deliberately left off the list of best cars for teen drivers for apparent safety concerns. “While some pickups and SUVs score well, they’re really not great choices for novice drivers,” says CarInsurance.com consumer analyst Penny Gusner.

query: list of the best suv cars for teens
sources:
[1] New SUVs that are safe for your family and teen driver include the midsize 2015 Toyota Highlander, as well as the compact 2015 Mazda CX-5, Mitsubishi Outlander (AWD only) and Subaru Forester. These SUVs are both IIHS Top Safety Pick+ recipients and have NHTSA's highest five-star overall rating.

[2] Safest Cars for Teens: SUVs. If a large, dull sedan isn't your teen's ideal first car, McCartt suggests shopping for an SUV. With ESC dramatically reducing rollover risk, the inherent advantages offered by SUVs' greater size, weight and height emerge more clearly, the IIHS says in its January 2015 status report.

[3] As icing on the proverbial cake, each of the models on the best cars for teen drivers list carries reasonably low car-insurance rates – or at least as far as teen drivers are concerned.

[4] We selected the 15 cars on this list the pillars of safety, reliability, and affordability. And despite what you might expect, not all the cars are compact and midsize sedans. A number of models, including large SUVs and a few sports cars, are suitable choices for first-time drivers.

[5] Toyota Celica. For many teens, owning a sports car is nothing more than a distant dream. But parents and teens can find the ultimate compromise in the Toyota Celica. Once they get over the shock of seeing a cassette player for the first time, teens will enjoy this car just as much as their parents did.

[6] Lifestyle 7/18/2014 @ 8:32PM 85,728 views. The Safest Used Cars For Teen Drivers. Teenagers are more likely than other drivers to have the least safe types of cars, often ending up behind the wheel of vehicles that are old, small and without good crash protection. Those are the findings of new research conducted by the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety, a nonprofit financed by the insurance industry.

[7] [Slideshow: Safest Cars for Teens] Teens that have their own vehicle drive their vehicle more and are more likely to be in a crash, just because of that, says Anne McCartt, senior vice president of research at the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety.

[8] To that end, the experts at CarInsurance.com recently compiled a list of 14 used cars that should be ideal for teen drivers; we’re featuring them in the accompanying slideshow with our own commentary. Each is from the 2009 model year and is valued at $15,000 or less according to Edmunds.com.

[9] Earlier this week the group released a list of recommended used vehicles to help parents buy safe cars within their budgets, ranging from less than $5,000 to nearly $20,000. “A teenager’s first car is more than just a financial decision,” Adrian Lund, the institute’s president, said in a statement.

[10] Note that pickups and sport-utility vehicles were deliberately left off the list of best cars for teen drivers for apparent safety concerns. “While some pickups and SUVs score well, they’re really not great choices for novice drivers,” says CarInsurance.com consumer analyst Penny Gusner.

query: list of the best suv cars for teens
sources:
[1] New SUVs that are safe for your family and teen driver include the midsize 2015 Toyota Highlander, as well as the compact 2015 Mazda CX-5, Mitsubishi Outlander (AWD only) and Subaru Forester. These SUVs are both IIHS Top Safety Pick+ recipients and have NHTSA's highest five-star overall rating.

[2] Safest Cars for Teens: SUVs. If a large, dull sedan isn't your teen's ideal first car, McCartt suggests shopping for an SUV. With ESC dramatically reducing rollover risk, the inherent advantages offered by SUVs' greater size, weight and height emerge more clearly, the IIHS says in its January 2015 status report.

[3] As icing on the proverbial cake, each of the models on the best cars for teen drivers list carries reasonably low car-insurance rates – or at least as far as teen drivers are concerned.

[4] We selected the 15 cars on this list the pillars of safety, reliability, and affordability. And despite what you might expect, not all the cars are compact and midsize sedans. A number of models, including large SUVs and a few sports cars, are suitable choices for first-time drivers.

[5] Toyota Celica. For many teens, owning a sports car is nothing more than a distant dream. But parents and teens can find the ultimate compromise in the Toyota Celica. Once they get over the shock of seeing a cassette player for the first time, teens will enjoy this car just as much as their parents did.

[6] Lifestyle 7/18/2014 @ 8:32PM 85,728 views. The Safest Used Cars For Teen Drivers. Teenagers are more likely than other drivers to have the least safe types of cars, often ending up behind the wheel of vehicles that are old, small and without good crash protection. Those are the findings of new research conducted by the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety, a nonprofit financed by the insurance industry.

[7] [Slideshow: Safest Cars for Teens] Teens that have their own vehicle drive their vehicle more and are more likely to be in a crash, just because of that, says Anne McCartt, senior vice president of research at the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety.

[8] To that end, the experts at CarInsurance.com recently compiled a list of 14 used cars that should be ideal for teen drivers; we’re featuring them in the accompanying slideshow with our own commentary. Each is from the 2009 model year and is valued at $15,000 or less according to Edmunds.com.

[9] Earlier this week the group released a list of recommended used vehicles to help parents buy safe cars within their budgets, ranging from less than $5,000 to nearly $20,000. “A teenager’s first car is more than just a financial decision,” Adrian Lund, the institute’s president, said in a statement.

[10] Note that pickups and sport-utility vehicles were deliberately left off the list of best cars for teen drivers for apparent safety concerns. “While some pickups and SUVs score well, they’re really not great choices for novice drivers,” says CarInsurance.com consumer analyst Penny Gusner.

query: list of the best suv cars for teens
sources:
[1] New SUVs that are safe for your family and teen driver include the midsize 2015 Toyota Highlander, as well as the compact 2015 Mazda CX-5, Mitsubishi Outlander (AWD only) and Subaru Forester. These SUVs are both IIHS Top Safety Pick+ recipients and have NHTSA's highest five-star overall rating.

[2] Safest Cars for Teens: SUVs. If a large, dull sedan isn't your teen's ideal first car, McCartt suggests shopping for an SUV. With ESC dramatically reducing rollover risk, the inherent advantages offered by SUVs' greater size, weight and height emerge more clearly, the IIHS says in its January 2015 status report.

[3] As icing on the proverbial cake, each of the models on the best cars for teen drivers list carries reasonably low car-insurance rates – or at least as far as teen drivers are concerned.

[4] We selected the 15 cars on this list the pillars of safety, reliability, and affordability. And despite what you might expect, not all the cars are compact and midsize sedans. A number of models, including large SUVs and a few sports cars, are suitable choices for first-time drivers.

[5] Toyota Celica. For many teens, owning a sports car is nothing more than a distant dream. But parents and teens can find the ultimate compromise in the Toyota Celica. Once they get over the shock of seeing a cassette player for the first time, teens will enjoy this car just as much as their parents did.

[6] Lifestyle 7/18/2014 @ 8:32PM 85,728 views. The Safest Used Cars For Teen Drivers. Teenagers are more likely than other drivers to have the least safe types of cars, often ending up behind the wheel of vehicles that are old, small and without good crash protection. Those are the findings of new research conducted by the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety, a nonprofit financed by the insurance industry.

[7] [Slideshow: Safest Cars for Teens] Teens that have their own vehicle drive their vehicle more and are more likely to be in a crash, just because of that, says Anne McCartt, senior vice president of research at the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety.

[8] To that end, the experts at CarInsurance.com recently compiled a list of 14 used cars that should be ideal for teen drivers; we’re featuring them in the accompanying slideshow with our own commentary. Each is from the 2009 model year and is valued at $15,000 or less according to Edmunds.com.

[9] Earlier this week the group released a list of recommended used vehicles to help parents buy safe cars within their budgets, ranging from less than $5,000 to nearly $20,000. “A teenager’s first car is more than just a financial decision,” Adrian Lund, the institute’s president, said in a statement.

[10] Note that pickups and sport-utility vehicles were deliberately left off the list of best cars for teen drivers for apparent safety concerns. “While some pickups and SUVs score well, they’re really not great choices for novice drivers,” says CarInsurance.com consumer analyst Penny Gusner.
